memory_candidates.content: jq gotcha: inside a pipeline like `$array | index(.field)`, the `.` inside index(...)'s argument is evaluated against $array (the piped-in value), NOT the outer context's current object. Binding the outer value to a named variable first (`. as $t | ... index($t.field) ...`) avoids 'Cannot index array with string' errors when building select() filters that need both the piped array and an outer object's field.

When embedding a multi-line jq program as a single-quoted bash string, ANY apostrophe in a comment or prose line inside that program (e.g. "the function's convention") silently terminates the bash single-quoted string early and produces a confusing 'syntax error near unexpected token' pointing at jq code, not the apostrophe. Grep the embedded program for stray apostrophes before debugging jq syntax when bash -n fails on a script containing an inline jq heredoc/string.

For a core script that must read specs/state.json exactly once and needs no other main input, use `jq -n -c --argjson X ... --slurpfile Y "$FILE" '...'` (note the `-n`) and do NOT also pass "$FILE" as a positional argument to jq -- that would cause a second read. The -n flag lets the whole jq program run against argjson/slurpfile-bound variables only.
